Project overview. The deck follows an academic project sequence and uses the supplied app screenshots as implementation evidence. The sample screenshots are illustrative demonstrations, not a controlled clinical validation study.

name: Rectangle 6
text: Driver fatigue can reduce attention and slow a driver’s response. A phone mounted to face the driver can observe visible cues such as eye closure, yawning, head nodding, and whether the face remains in view.

name: Rectangle 10
text: A practical warning system should track how long the eyes remain closed and how often prolonged episodes occur, while handling missing camera evidence explicitly.

name: Rectangle 14
text: Use a standard phone camera and local processing to provide immediate feedback without sending face images to a server.

name: Rectangle 18
text: DriveSafe is a driver-awareness aid. It does not diagnose fatigue or replace rest, safe driving decisions, or professional validation.

name: Rectangle 19
text: The app presents live measurements and escalating alerts in a compact dashboard.
Project context is based on the reviewed DriveSafe Android source. CameraX provides preview and image analysis use cases [3].

name: Rectangle 9
text: Landmark distances summarize eye openness in each frame. Temporal changes help distinguish a short blink from a prolonged closure. EAR is a geometric signal, not a direct measure of alertness [1].

name: Rectangle 13
text: Percentage of eye-closure time over a rolling window provides a time-based cue associated with visual attention lapses [2]. This app computes a valid-observation variant over 30 seconds.

name: Rectangle 13
text: Eye shape, camera angle, and face proportions differ. Calibration estimates a personal open-eye baseline, reducing dependence on one global EAR cutoff.

name: Rectangle 14
text: Calibration uses a 3.5-second sample window, at least 20 valid samples per eye, and a near-frontal head pose. It trims low and high outliers, then sets per-eye thresholds at 65% (closed) and 80% (open) of baseline.

name: Rectangle 30
text: A reopening shorter than 250 ms does not end the active closure episode. Episode history rolls over 45 seconds.
Implementation values from CalibrationManager.kt and ClosureEpisodeTracker.kt. EAR formulation follows the landmark-ratio concept in [1]. Threshold labels reproduce the app’s DurationCategory values.
How the drowsiness score is calculated
Final score = clamp(0, 100, 0.40 × closure score + 0.25 × PERCLOS score + 0.20 × prolonged-closure frequency score + 0.15 × average episode score + current yawn bonus + current nod bonus)
Each component is scored from 0 to 100 before weighting.
Longer current closure raises this component. A closure of 2 seconds reaches its maximum.
Closed-eye time ÷ valid observed eye time in the last 30 seconds. It needs 5 seconds of valid data; unknown gaps are skipped.
Counts closures of at least 500 ms in a rolling 45-second window: 0→0, 1→30, 2→65, 3 or more→100.
Uses recent completed episodes: 150 ms or less maps to 0; 600 ms or more maps to 100, with linear scaling between.
+12 for each new event, up to 25.
+15 for each new event, up to 30.
Both bonuses fade by 15% per processed frame.
Weighted total plus current event bonuses, capped at 100.

The four weighted components and event bonuses are implemented in DrowsinessScoringEngine.kt. PERCLOS timing and missing-data behavior are in PerclosCalculator.kt. Prolonged-episode history is in ClosureEpisodeTracker.kt. Each component contributes a weighted amount; yawns and nods add temporary bonuses after the weighted sum. The final score is clamped to 0–100.
Either the score threshold or the closure-duration threshold can trigger the higher alert state.
Escalation happens immediately. Downgrading an alert requires 1.5 seconds of confirmed open-eye observations.
After face lock, 1.5 seconds without a visible face triggers its own critical warning. Missing face data does not add to the drowsiness score.

Thresholds and recovery hysteresis are implemented in DrowsinessScoringEngine.kt. Face lock and independent face-loss timing are in FaceVisibilityTracker.kt. Critical alert playback and warning cooldown are coordinated by DrowsinessDetector.kt and AlertManager.kt.
